title: Hemoglobin Trend in Upper GI Bleed
scenario: A 55-year-old client admitted with hematemesis and melena from a suspected upper gastrointestinal bleed is monitored with serial hemoglobin levels and vital signs over eight hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the trend shown on the flowsheet?

options.text: The falling hemoglobin with rising pulse and falling blood pressure indicates ongoing active bleeding
The hemoglobin is stable and the client is compensating well
The changes reflect hemodilution from intravenous fluids only
The trend indicates resolving hemorrhage and improving perfusion

questions.rationale: Hemoglobin dropped from 11.2 to 7.6 g/dL while pulse rose and blood pressure fell with cool, clammy skin, a pattern of continued blood loss and early hypovolemic shock rather than stability or resolution.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Given the deteriorating trend, which interventions should the nurse anticipate or implement? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider of the worsening trend immediately
Prepare to administer a blood transfusion
Ensure large-bore IV access and infuse isotonic fluids as ordered
Type and crossmatch the client for packed red blood cells
Withhold IV fluids to avoid diluting the blood further

questions.rationale: Active bleeding with signs of hypovolemic shock requires prompt provider notification, volume resuscitation through large-bore access, and preparation for transfusion after type and crossmatch. Withholding fluids or delaying reassessment would worsen shock.
